FROMGIT: drm/msm: Fix NULL deref on bind/probe deferral This patch avoids dereferencing msm_host->dev when it is NULL. If we find ourselves tearing down dsi before calling (mdp4|mdp5|dpu)_kms_init(), we'll end up in a state where the dev pointer is NULL and trying to extract priv from it will fail. This was introduced in a seemingly innocuous commit to ensure the arguments to msm_gem_put_iova() are correct (even though that function has been a stub for ~5 years). UPSTREAM: util/cbfstool: Support FIT payloads In order to support booting a GNU/Linux payload on non x86, the FIT format should be used, as it is the defacto standard on ARM. Due to greater complexity of FIT it is not converted to simple ELF format. Add support for autodecting FIT payloads and add them as new CBFS_TYPE 'fit'. The payload is included as is, with no special header. The code can determine the type at runtime using the CBFS_TYPE field. Support for parsing FIT payloads in coreboot is added in a follow on commit. Compression of FIT payloads is not supported, as the FIT sections might be compressed itself. Starting at this point a CBFS payload/ can be either of type FIT or SELF. Tested on Cavium SoC. use action descriptor when programming flash chips The second attempt. The original patch did not allow partial erase of layout sections. To fix it this patch changes the following: - when invoking handle_romentries() pass it the erase mode flag. In erase mode do not read the input file contents for the section(s), specified by the user. This results in the section(s) contents remaining filled with the erase byte values. Added a comment header in layout.h to explain this. - with the above change erase_chip() becomes even simpler, as it does not need to create a fake new contents buffer, it uses whatever was prepared by handle_romentries() - moved the new added read logging into debug level instead of info. The original patch description: This patch makes use of action descriptor structure introduced earlier. The array of processing units is created based on comparing of old (when available) and new flashrom contents. The new scheme has a few advantages which are especially noticeable when programming mode limits the clock rate at which the flash chip is operated (namely raiden driver): - when there is a need to erase part of the chip, the largest feasible erase size unit is used. This speeds up processing quite a bit in many cases. - if user enters --fast-verify in the command line, only areas written in the current session are verified, even if the user did specify any layout areas explicitly. - when both --erase_chip and --do-not-diff are included in the command line, the chip is erased using the largest possible erase size instead of reading its contents first to determine if some areas are already erased. platform_Flashrom: account for unibuild firmware tarballs The platform_Flashrom test at one point tries to reprogram the DUT flash device with the BIOS image from chromeos-firmwareupdate self extracting archive. The test expects to see the bios.bin file in the top level directory created when the tarball is unpacked. With recent introduction of the unibuild there could be multiple bios images in the same tarball, located in the models subdirectory. This patch modifies the test to use the FirmwareUpdater() class to properly locate the bios image matching the model the test is running on. Also removed the unused re import, as suggested by the linter. BRANCH=none BUG=b:79492818 TEST=verified that platform_Flashrom test passes on Fizz(unibuild) and Pyro(single bios.bin). chromeos_config: Require all non-slaves to be important. Instead of playing whack-a-mole to make sure all non-slave builds appear as important in Legoland, add a unittest to ensure they are. Further, change the default for 'important' to be True, not False. Since many configs will become important with this change, I added logic to a unittest that dumps all unimportant slave configs. cryptohome: Reduce use of SecureBlob in BootAttributes. Polymorphic usage of SecureBlob is problematic (see crbug.com/728047). BootAttributes is using SecureBlobs in places that don't really require it. In preparation for making SecureBlob not inherit from brillo::Blob (which would break some of these usages), reduce use of SecureBlob. BootAttributes are meant to be tamper-evident, not read-protected. Therefore we don't really need to read the data into a SecureBlob. Public keys also don't need to be SecureBlobs, nor does any signed data. Replace all of these to be plain Blobs. Signatures technically don't need to be SecureBlobs either (they're just encrypted hashes), but the existing TPM API makes it annoying to pass Blobs as signatures. To avoid having to do extra conversions, keep signatures as SecureBlobs. The Service class exposes methods that used to take a SecureBlob (and now take Blobs), but those methods are not used outside of the class, so they can also be updated in this CL. BUG=chromium:728047 TEST=cryptohome unit tests still pass on samus and eve. TEST=eve boots. TEST=kevin boots.
